MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which number is written in words as "four thousand, six hundred and five"? (1 mark)
   A. 4,065
   B. 465
   C. 46,005
   D. 4,605

2. What is the total value of the digit 9 in 6,092? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 10
   C. 90
   D. 9

3. Which number is written in words as "nine thousand and ten"? (1 mark)
   A. 90,100
   B. 9,010
   C. 910
   D. 9,100

4. Which of these is a multiple of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 86
   B. 84
   C. 83
   D. 85

5. Round 128 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 120
   B. 100
   C. 140
   D. 130

6. Work out 4,236 + 1,528. (1 mark)
   A. 5,754
   B. 5,664
   C. 5,764
   D. 5,774

7. Which number must be added to 1,500 to make 6,000? (1 mark)
   A. 4,600
   B. 7,500
   C. 4,490
   D. 4,500

8. What is the next number in the pattern 10,000, 9,000, 8,000, 7,000, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 6,000
   B. 5,000
   C. 9,000
   D. 7,000

9. Work out 8,500 − 3,275. (1 mark)
   A. 5,225
   B. 5,125
   C. 5,375
   D. 5,235

10. When multiplying 24 × 35, why do we write a zero in the ones place of the second partial product? (1 mark)
   A. Because 35 ends in 5
   B. Because we are multiplying by 30, which is 3 tens
   C. To make the answer bigger
   D. Because 24 ends in 4

11. What is 60 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 160
   B. 600
   C. 60,000
   D. 6,000

12. What is 99 × 100? (1 mark)
   A. 9,900
   B. 99,000
   C. 990
   D. 199

13. What is 58 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 14 remainder 2
   B. 13 remainder 6
   C. 14 remainder 3
   D. 15 remainder 2

14. What is 38 ÷ 5? (1 mark)
   A. 6 remainder 8
   B. 7 remainder 3
   C. 7 remainder 4
   D. 8 remainder 3

15. What is 200 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 3
   C. 200
   D. 2

16. 59 mangoes are shared equally among 8 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 3
   C. 4
   D. 5

17. Dan writes some more fractions. Which of these is an improper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 4 2/3
   B. 8/3
   C. 1/2
   D. 3/8

18. A circle is cut into 5 equal parts and 2 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 2/5
   B. 5/3
   C. 3/2
   D. 3/5

19. Beth writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 9/9
   B. 2/9
   C. 3 1/2
   D. 11/5

20. In the fraction 7/10, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 17
   C. 3
   D. 10

21. What is 5/12 of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 12
   C. 10
   D. 14

22. Which decimal is the same as 1/2? (1 mark)
   A. 0.5
   B. 0.12
   C. 0.2
   D. 2.0

23. In the number 5.68, the digit 6 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Hundredths
   B. Tens
   C. Ones
   D. Tenths

24. Write 3/10 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.13
   B. 0.03
   C. 0.3
   D. 3.0

25. If x = 10, what is the value of x ÷ 2 + 1? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 6
   C. 1
   D. 11

26. Simplify 7x − 4x. (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 28x
   C. 11x
   D. 3x

27. Change 375 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 75 cm
   B. 37 cm
   C. 4 m 25 cm
   D. 4 m 75 cm

28. What is the perimeter of a shape? (1 mark)
   A. The number of its corners
   B. The distance all the way round its edge
   C. Its longest side
   D. The space inside it

29. A rectangle is made of 3 rows with 5 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 18 square units
   B. 8 square units
   C. 16 square units
   D. 15 square units

30. Which unit is used for area? (1 mark)
   A. Centimetres
   B. Litres
   C. Kilograms
   D. Square centimetres

31. A rectangle is made of 8 rows with 12 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 96 square units
   B. 104 square units
   C. 40 square units
   D. 20 square units

32. The unit for volume when each block has sides of 1 cm is (1 mark)
   A. square centimetres
   B. litres
   C. centimetres
   D. cubic centimetres

33. A box is 10 cm long, 10 cm wide and 10 cm high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 300 cubic centimetres
   B. 100 cubic centimetres
   C. 1,000 cubic centimetres
   D. 30 cubic centimetres

34. What is 3 1/2 L + 1 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 5 1/4 L
   B. 5 L
   C. 4 1/2 L
   D. 4 3/4 L

35. Which is the best instrument for comparing the mass of a mango with known masses? (1 mark)
   A. A measuring jug
   B. A clock
   C. A beam balance
   D. A ruler

36. a.m. is used for times (1 mark)
   A. from noon to midnight
   B. only at night
   C. only at midday
   D. from midnight to noon

37. How many hours are in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 168 hours
   B. 84 hours
   C. 192 hours
   D. 420 hours

38. How many cents are in Ksh 40? (1 mark)
   A. 40,000 cents
   B. 140 cents
   C. 4,000 cents
   D. 400 cents

39. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. How many are NOT pawpaw? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 9
   C. 1
   D. 10

40. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. How many are dog or hen together? (1 mark)
   A. 4
   B. 3
   C. 5
   D. 6

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Wanjiru buys 4 loaves of bread at Ksh 60 each, 2 packets of sugar at Ksh 155 each and 1 tin of cooking fat at Ksh 480. She pays with Ksh 2,000. (a) Find the total cost. (b) Find her change. (5 marks)

42. Change 3 hours to minutes and 2 days to hours. (2 marks)

43. Draw an angle using a ruler. Name the vertex and the arms and mark the angle with a small curve. (3 marks)

44. Ksh 3.50 is given as 3 shillings and 50 cents. Write 75 cents and 5 cents as decimals of a shilling. (3 marks)

45. Divide 84 by 4 and check your answer. (3 marks)

46. A ribbon is 5 m 20 cm long. A piece 2 m 75 cm long is cut off. How much ribbon is left? (3 marks)

47. Express 23/6 as a mixed fraction. (3 marks)

48. Add 4,236 and 1,528. Show your working. (3 marks)

49. Ten vehicles passed: 5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses and 1 lorry. Draw a table to show this data. (3 marks)

50. Work out 6 1/4 kg − 2 3/4 kg. (3 marks)

51. Add 3,568 and 2,276 and say how many times you regrouped. (3 marks)

52. Write the steps for collecting and recording data about the favourite colours of 10 friends. (4 marks)

53. A box is packed with cubes in layers. Each layer has 8 cubes along the length and 5 cubes across the width. There are 4 layers. (a) How many cubes are in one layer? (b) What is the volume of the packed cubes? (c) If 30 cubes are taken out, how many cubes are left? (5 marks)

54. Work out 4,000 − 1,236. Show how you regroup. (3 marks)

55. Work out 36 × 24 by first multiplying by the ones and then by the tens. (3 marks)

56. Write 2 25/100 and 5 7/100 as decimals. (2 marks)

57. A water tank holds 1,000 litres. Each day the family uses 125 litres. Write the amount left after 1, 2 and 3 days. (3 marks)

58. A 20 L jerrycan is used to fill 5 L buckets. How many buckets can be filled? How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from one bucket? (4 marks)

59. A bag has a mass of 5 kg. Musa takes out 1 1/2 kg of beans. What mass is left in the bag? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 4,605
   four thousand, six hundred and five: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 4,605.

2. C — 90
   The digit 9 is in the tens place, so its total value is 9 × 10 = 90.

3. B — 9,010
   nine thousand and ten: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 9,010.

4. B — 84
   84 = 12 × 7, so 84 is a multiple of 12.

5. D — 130
   Look at the ones digit 8. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 128 rounds to 130.

6. C — 5,764
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 4,236 + 1,528 = 5,764.

7. D — 4,500
   6,000 − 1,500 = 4,500. Check: 1,500 + 4,500 = 6,000.

8. A — 6,000
   The rule is subtract 1,000. 7,000 − 1,000 = 6,000.

9. A — 5,225
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225. Check: 5,225 + 3,275 = 8,500.

10. B — Because we are multiplying by 30, which is 3 tens
   24 × 30 = 24 × 3 × 10 = 720, so the ones place holds a 0.

11. D — 6,000
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 60 × 100 = 6,000.

12. A — 9,900
   Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 99 × 100 = 9,900.

13. A — 14 remainder 2
   4 × 14 = 56 and 58 − 56 = 2. So 58 ÷ 4 = 14 remainder 2. Check: 14 × 4 + 2 = 58.

14. B — 7 remainder 3
   5 × 7 = 35 and 38 − 35 = 3. So 38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. Check: 7 × 5 + 3 = 38.

15. D — 2
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 200 ÷ 100 = 2.

16. B — 3
   59 ÷ 8 = 7 remainder 3. Each child gets 7 and 3 are left.

17. B — 8/3
   In an improper fraction the numerator is equal to or bigger than the denominator. 8/3 is one whole or more.

18. D — 3/5
   Not shaded: 5 − 2 = 3 parts, so 3/5.

19. B — 2/9
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 2/9 is less than one whole.

20. D — 10
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

21. C — 10
   24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 2 × 5 = 10. So 5/12 of 24 is 10.

22. A — 0.5
   1/2 = 5/10 = 0.5.

23. D — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 5.68 the digit 6 is in the tenths place.

24. C — 0.3
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 3/10 = 0.3.

25. B — 6
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 6.

26. D — 3x
   Only like terms can be joined. 7x − 4x = 3x.

27. A — 3 m 75 cm
   375 ÷ 100 = 3 remainder 75. So 375 cm = 3 m 75 cm.

28. B — The distance all the way round its edge
   Perimeter is the total length of all the sides.

29. D — 15 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 3 × 5 = 15 square units.

30. D — Square centimetres
   Area is measured in square units, such as square centimetres (cm²).

31. A — 96 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 8 × 12 = 96 square units.

32. D — cubic centimetres
   Each block is one cubic centimetre, so volume is measured in cubic centimetres.

33. C — 1,000 cubic centimetres
   10 × 10 = 100 per layer and 100 × 10 = 1,000 cubic centimetres.

34. D — 4 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 1/2 L + 1 1/4 L = 4 3/4 L.

35. C — A beam balance
   A beam balance compares an object with known masses.

36. D — from midnight to noon
   a.m. is used from midnight to noon and p.m. from noon to midnight.

37. A — 168 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 7 × 24 = 168 hours.

38. C — 4,000 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 40 = 40 × 100 = 4,000 cents.

39. B — 9
   10 − 1 = 9.

40. C — 5
   3 + 2 = 5.

SECTION B
----
41. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 1,030 (b) Ksh 970
   Working / marking points: 4 × 60 = 240 (1 mark); 2 × 155 = 310 (1 mark); 240 + 310 + 480 = 1,030 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,030 = 970 (2 marks).

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: 180 minutes and 48 hours
   Working / marking points: 3 × 60 = 180 (1 mark); 2 × 24 = 48 (1 mark).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with two straight lines meeting at a point, the point labelled vertex, the lines labelled arms and a curve between them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two straight arms, 1 mark for the vertex, 1 mark for the curve.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.75 and 0.05 of a shilling (Ksh 0.75 and Ksh 0.05)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the idea that 100 cents = 1 shilling, 1 mark for each decimal.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 21
   Working / marking points: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 (1 mark); 4 ÷ 4 = 1, so 21 (1 mark); check 21 × 4 = 84 (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 45 cm
   Working / marking points: 520 − 275 = 245 cm (2 marks); 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm (1 mark).

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 5/6
   Working / marking points: 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5 (2 marks). Write 3 5/6 with the same denominator (1 mark).

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,764
   Working / marking points: Ones 6 + 8 = 14, write 4 carry 1 (1 mark); tens 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 (1 mark); hundreds 2 + 5 = 7, thousands 4 + 1 = 5, answer 5,764 (1 mark).

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: A table with a title and two columns, Vehicle and Number, with rows matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1 and total 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for title and headings, 1 mark for all four rows correct, 1 mark for the total 10.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 3/4 = 1/2 (1 mark); answer 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,844. You regrouped twice (ones to tens, tens to hundreds).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct sum, 1 mark for the carries, 1 mark for saying twice.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the question; ask each friend and make a tally mark; draw a table with a title and headings; write the totals and check they add up to 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 40 cubes (b) 160 cubes (c) 130 cubes
   Working / marking points: (a) 8 × 5 = 40 (1 mark); (b) 40 × 4 = 160 (2 marks); (c) 160 − 30 = 130 (2 marks).

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2,764
   Working / marking points: Borrow from the thousands so the number is 3 thousands 9 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones (1 mark). 10 − 6 = 4, 9 − 3 = 6, 9 − 2 = 7, 3 − 1 = 2 (1 mark). Answer 2,764 (1 mark).

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 864
   Working / marking points: 36 × 4 = 144 (1 mark); 36 × 20 = 720 (1 mark); 144 + 720 = 864 (1 mark).

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2.25 and 5.07
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal. 5 7/100 needs a 0 in the tenths place.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 875 litres, 750 litres, 625 litres
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct amount.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 buckets; 20 cups
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks); 5 × 4 = 20 cups (2 marks).

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 5 − 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.
